slides.title: Binary Search Trees
slides.main: A search tree keeps order, which a hash table lacks, and changes quickly.

captions: Sorted array: ordered, but an insert shifts half of it
Hash table: fast, but no order or ranges
Search tree: search, insert, and order in time of the height

body.text: Fourteen exercises: from insertion and deletion to a pair with a sum using two iterators.

slides.title: The rule
slides.main: The condition covers all descendants, so check with bounds, not children.

captions: At every node: smaller on the left, larger on the right
The condition covers all descendants, not just the children
Inorder traversal gives keys in ascending order
Node 7 is smaller than parent 3? No, but it is right of 5, still larger than it, yet sits on the left: tree broken

frames.text: all right of 3 in its subtree > 3

slides.title: Search
slides.main: Each step discards a whole subtree; the cost is the tree height.

captions: Looking for 6: 6 < 8, go left
6 > 3, go right
6 = 6, found in 3 comparisons
Looking for 5: 8 → 3 → 6 → 4 → empty link: no such key

slides.title: Insertion
slides.main: Other nodes are not touched: no shifting, the cost is the height.

captions: Inserting 5: descend as in search
4 has nothing on the right: hang the new node there
Other nodes untouched: no shifting, the cost is the tree height

slides.title: Minimum, maximum, successor
slides.main: The successor is the minimum of the right subtree or the nearest ancestor on the left.

captions: The minimum is the leftmost node
The maximum is the rightmost
6 has a right subtree: the successor is its minimum, which is 7
7 has nothing on the right: the successor is the nearest ancestor for which we are on the left (that is 8)

slides.title: Deletion
slides.main: A node with two children is replaced by its successor, and the successor is removed from its old place.

captions: Three deletion cases; let's start with this tree
A leaf (7) is simply cut off
Node 14 with one child (13): the child takes its place
Node 3 with two children: take the successor (4), copy the key, and delete the successor from the right subtree

slides.title: Degeneration
slides.main: Sorted insertions turn the tree into a list: O(n).

captions: Keys came in random order: height about 1.5 log₂ n
Keys came in ascending order: each new one is rightmost
The tree became a list: search is O(n). Balancing is needed

slides.title: Range queries
slides.main: Time is the height plus the number of keys found.

captions: All keys from 4 to 10: start at the root
3 is less than 4: skip its left subtree (node 1) entirely
14 is greater than 10: skip the right subtree of node 10
Found 4, 6, 7, 8, 10: time is the height plus the number of answers

slides.title: Floor, ceiling, k-th
slides.main: Nearest keys are found in one descent, remembering the turns.

captions: Floor of 5 is the largest key ≤ 5: remember nodes where we turned right (3, then 4)
Ceiling of 5 is the smallest key ≥ 5: remember where we turned left (8, then 6)
k-th: inorder traversal with a stop: 1, 3, 4, so the answer is 4

slides.title: Comparing structures
slides.main: Need order: tree; need only access: hash; rarely changes: array.

captions: Array: best for rare changes and reading
Hash: when only access by key is needed
Unbalanced tree: order is there, but the height is unpredictable
Balanced tree: the ordered dictionary in Java and C++

slides.title: Rotations
slides.main: A rotation changes the height, but not the key order.

captions: The right subtree is heavier: root 3 with right child 6
6 goes up, 3 goes down to the left; the left subtree of 6 (node 4) moves to node 3
Key order is the same (1 3 4 6 7), the height got smaller. The cost is a few links

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: Bounds instead of children, one duplicate policy, removing the successor.

captions: Checking validity by children alone misses violations deeper down
If insertion puts equal keys on the right, search must look for them on the right
When deleting a node with two children, remember to remove the successor, or you get a duplicate
Empty tree, one node, a chain, deleting the root and a node with two children
